_comment: Reviewed non-matches for the `border` family in vocabulary.ts's RETIRED scan. RETIRED.border flags a bare `border`/`border-b`/`border-t`/`border-l`/`border-r` between word-boundary delimiters (space/quote/backtick/brace) so it can find real Tailwind class strings — but that same rule cannot tell a class string apart from English prose, a comment, a JSDoc line, a test description, or a data/enum string literal (e.g. `'text' | 'border'`). Every entry below was read in its surrounding context and confirmed to be one of those, never a border-width utility. This ratchet mechanism is shared: `radius-baseline.json` holds the same kind of reviewed non-matches for the `radius` family (bare `rounded` colliding with the English word or a local identifier), kept as a separate file rather than nested under this one because `readBaseline()` hard-validates `{ violations: string[] }` as a flat array. Both baselines must only ever shrink: fixing the scanner to correctly exclude a shape removes entries here, and any new source hit that isn't already the exact text of an existing entry is a real, unswept site — never add an entry to hide one, and never reword or rename working source just to make an entry unnecessary. Hand-maintained by design: there is no `--update-baseline` regeneration path, on purpose — every addition here should come from someone reading the line in context and confirming it isn't a class string, not from a script accepting whatever the scanner currently reports.
